title.narrative: Centre of excellence in scent detection animals in Morogoro, Tanzania

description.narrative: An African Center of Excellence in Tanzania specialized in scent detection animals, with the human, animal, and technological capacity to develop and implement scent detection solutions that protect people and the environment, such as the detection of TB and landmines.

Immediate target groups are the scent detection animal experts, including trainers, technical advisors, and researchers in animal learning, behavior and olfaction. Ultimate beneficiaries will be vulnerable communities affected by TB (mainly impoverished city slum dwellers); landmines (impoverished rural communities unable to farm their land); and environmental havoc (such as victims of earthquakes and people living in contaminated environments).

The outcome of this project will be an African Centre of Excellence in Tanzania, specialized in scent detection animals. It will build the human, animal, and technological capacity to develop and implement solutions for the detection of tuberculosis (TB) and other applications that protect people and the environment. SUA-APOPO supplies TB detection rats to Tanzania and Ethiopia, and landmine detection rats to Cambodia and Angola. We also develop new applications for areas like disaster preparedness, such as Search and Rescue Rats which can locate trapped survivors following disasters; health diagnosis, such as the detection of Brucella; and environmental purposes, such as the detection of endangered wildlife smuggled to the far east and contaminated soils to facilitate environmental clean-up. Scent detection animal training is underdeveloped in Africa, while its inputs of knowledge, labour, and carefully selected animals are affordable and sustainable. In collaboration with the Sokoine University of Agriculture (SUA), APOPO will develop the necessary curriculum and knowledge base to provide a sustainable capacity for this new regional industry, creating more independence from imported technology and expertise. During the program implementation period, SUA-APOPO aims to expand its research and operational partnerships with the goal of becoming a Centre of Excellence and an African focal point for scent detection animals. The final outcome should benefit the vulnerable communities affected by TB, explosive remnants of war, and environmental risks, including those caused by climate change. APOPO aims to bring a service model where a technology developed by the local population serves the needs of the local populations.

participating-org.narrative: Direction-Générale Coopération au Développement et Aide humanitaire

description.narrative: RESULT 1: Sufficient capacity of people and scent detection animals.

title.narrative: Result 1, Indictor 1: Number of qualified animal trainers, technical advisors, and lab technicians trained.

baseline.value: 67 total trainers/handlers. Tanzania = 23 (7 women); International = 44 (13 women; 3 Technical Advisors; 23 Cambodians; 7 Angolan; 6 Ethiopian; 5 Mozambican)

target.value: 120 total trainers/handlers. Tanzania = 45 (≥18 women); International = 75 (≥25 women)

title.narrative: Result 1, Indicator 2: Number of qualified scent detection animals trained and/or deployed and total training center capacity.

baseline.value: 72 total rats trained and/or deployed and accredited: Tanzania = 49 (19 TB),); International = 53 (10 Ethiopia, 34 Cambodia, 9 Angola). The training center has the capacity to deliver 30 fully trained rats per year.

target.value: ≥ 90 total rats trained and/or deployed and accredited: Tanzania ≥ 60; International ≥ 70. The training center has the capacity to deliver ≥ 40 fully trained rats per year.

description.narrative: RESULT 2: Improvement of existing solutions and development of new detection solutions.

title.narrative: Result 2, Indicator 1: Improved accuracy and efficiency of TB detection rats.

baseline.value: 81.3% sensitivity, 73.4% specificity (Kanaan, et al., 2021. Rats sniff out pulmonary tuberculosis from sputum: A diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis. Nature: Scientific Reports, 11 doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-81086-x )

description.narrative: RESULT 3: A regional knowledge-base in scent detection animals.

title.narrative: Result 3, Indictor 1: Curriculum in learning and behavior formulated.

baseline.value: In-house training package including curriculum, practical, and tests formulated.

target.value: Training package with curriculum, practical, and tests remains in use.
